brief.summary: Equities stabilized into the Fed decision, S&P futures up modestly while credit spreads stayed super tight despite heavy supply. Front-end yields have repriced roughly 30-40bp since late July, two-year near 4.65%, while the ten-year flirts with 5% and the thirty-year rose only about 17bp, flattening the curve. Markets price near-certain odds of a 25bp hike, the first since 2023, with three to four hikes implied over the next year and a hawkish dot plot expected. Guests warn of a policy error and a credibility premium around Chair Warsh, with the long end the key test. Crude fell about 1% on supply-disruption headlines; gold and the dollar were not discussed directionally. Tone is cautious, not risk-on.
notable_quotes: It'd be quite a surprise if they did not hike.
You can't pretend rate hikes are great for risk assets. They just aren't.
